title: Quarter Sprint Playbook: Dedicated Pool Autoscale Readiness & Measurement
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Purpose: create a tightly scoped, repeatable quarterly playbook to take a Dedicated pool autoscale capability from pilot through operational readiness and measurable OKRs. This ticket synthesizes product goals, measurement plans, required engineering workstreams, and an ops handoff checklist so that each quarter we can run a rapid experiment -> rollout cycle with clear rollback and cost guardrails. The playbook will cover policy definitions (prewarm, fastpath, hedged reservations), canary criteria, SLO/latency targets, cost thresholds, and success metrics for rollout to customer-facing Dedicated SKUs.
acceptance_criteria: Draft playbook created with step-by-step run steps for pilot -> canary -> full rollout
Measurement dashboard queries defined (latency P50/P95, cost per 1M tokens, hit rate on warm pool) with Grafana/Console links
Engineering workstreams and owners identified with estimates and sprint mapping (ENG tickets linked)
Rollback and graceful degradation play defined with specific model fallback mapping and traffic shift steps
Runbook for oncall and SRE ops with run thresholds and postmortem template is added
milestones: Kickoff + alignment with Eng, SRE, Pricing (2026-02-15)
Full rollout gating review + ops signoff (2026-04-28)
metrics: Latency SLOs: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 250ms for 2048 context workloads
Cost guardrail: incremental cost per 1M tokens <= 8% above baseline for burst windows
Warm-pool hit rate target: >= 70% for prewarmed request patterns
Failure budget consumption: < 5% during canary windows
risks: Dedicated pool prewarm underestimates leading to higher token cost during bursts
Telemetry gaps for identifying prefix cache effectiveness
Model variant fallbacks might cause quality regressions for specific customer prompts
Inter-team coordination slippage (billing, SRE, sales enablement)
